newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound eight Palestinians in Hebron clash.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound eight Palestinians in Hebron clash.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded eight Palestinians in the third straight day of clashes with stone-throwing Arabs in the divided West Bank town of Hebron on Monday, witnesses and hospital officials said.
They said about 100 youths hurled stones, one home-made bomb and a petrol bomb at Israeli soldiers dressed in riot gear along the line that divides Hebron into Israeli and PLO-controlled areas.
Israel Radio said one Israeli soldier was hit by a stone and lightly wounded. Troops responded with rubber bullets.

Medics at Hebron's Alia hospital said eight Palestinians arrived with rubbler bullet wounds, including an 11-year-old boy who had been shot four times in the chest and face. They said he was undergoing surgery.
Palestinians said troops had not been using tear gas to quell demonstrations on request from the city's 400 Jewish settlers who had complained the fumes were bothering them.
An Israeli army spokeswoman confirmed that clashes were in progress in Hebron but gave no details.

Israeli soldiers shot and wounded dozens of Palestinians on Saturday and Sunday during clashes that erupted over a recent U.S. House of Representatives vote calling on President Bill Clinton to recognise Arab East Jerusalem as part of Israel's undivided capital.
Earlier on Monday, the PLO's senior official in Jerusalem, Faisal al-Husseini, and Palestinian legislators demonstrated outside the American Consulate in East Jerusalem to protest the U.S. vote.
The unrest underscored the fragility of Israel-PLO peace moves, deadlocked since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem three months ago.
Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January under an interim peace deal but kept troops in parts of the town to protect the settler enclaves.
